knowledge_fragments.content: Presentation: A 15-year-old female presented to the paediatrics outpatient department with progressive abnormal jerky body movements, difficulty walking, episodes of falling, and unusual behaviour over the past 18 months. There was no similar history in the family. The child had received all age-appropriate immunizations. Physical examination showed myoclonic jerks, increased muscle tone in all four limbs, reduced deep tendon reflexes, muscle strength of 5/5, and normal sensory system evaluation.. Confirmed diagnosis: Subacute Sclerosing Panencephalitis. Differential diagnosis includes: Subacute Sclerosing Panencephalitis.
knowledge_fragments.title: Case report: Subacute Sclerosing Panencephalitis

knowledge_fragments.content: Subacute onset of sarcoidosis is characterized instead by vanished and non-specific signs and symptoms such as fever, asthenia, weight loss and peripheral lymphadenopathies for less than two years. Here differential diagnosis is impossible on the basis of the clinical picture only.
knowledge_fragments.title: Clinical Features, Histopathology and Differential Diagnosis of Sarcoidosis. > 1. Introduction

knowledge_fragments.content: Presentation: A 36-year-old male presented with shortness of breath and swelling in the lower extremities for the past 2 weeks. The patient also reported experiencing intermittent fever over the last 2 months. Upon admission, vital signs included a heart rate of 103 beats per minute, blood pressure of 122/47 mmHg, and a temperature of 37.2°C. Cardiac examination identified a pandiastolic murmur in the aortic region. Laboratory tests indicated an elevated NT-proBNP level of 4492.0 pg/mL.. Confirmed diagnosis: Subacute Bacterial Endocarditis. Differential diagnosis includes: Subacute Bacterial Endocarditis.
knowledge_fragments.title: Case report: Subacute Bacterial Endocarditis

knowledge_fragments.content: Presentation: A 71-year-old male from Madrid, Spain, presented with a 2-month history of dysphonia. He has a 30-year history of smoking and underwent a liver transplant 8 years ago due to liver cirrhosis, currently on chronic immunosuppressant therapy with mycophenolate mofetil. The patient exhibited symptoms including dysphonia, dysphagia, odynophagia, autophony, fatigue, anorexia, and a weight loss of over 20 kg in the past 6 months. Fiber-optic laryngoscopy identified a vegetative lesion on the lingual surface of the epiglottis, extending to the epiglottic vallecula. A non-contrast computed tomography (CT) scan showed increased soft tissue size on the lingual surface of the epiglottis.. Confirmed diagnosis: Subacute Histoplasmosis. Differential diagnosis includes: Subacute Histoplasmosis.
knowledge_fragments.title: Case report: Subacute Histoplasmosis

knowledge_fragments.content: AIP is a severe, rapidly progressive form of IIP. The short-term mortality rate is 50% or more, and there is no proven treatment. It usually affects previously healthy individuals who develop rapidly progressive respiratory failure.

knowledge_fragments.content: Presentation: A 71-year-old male from Madrid, Spain, presented with a 2-month history of dysphonia. He has a 30-year history of smoking and underwent a liver transplant 8 years ago due to liver cirrhosis, currently on chronic immunosuppressant therapy with mycophenolate mofetil. The patient exhibited symptoms including dysphonia, dysphagia, odynophagia, autophony, fatigue, anorexia, and a weight loss of over 20 kg in the past 6 months. Fiber-optic laryngoscopy identified a vegetative lesion on the lingual surface of the epiglottis, extending to the epiglottic vallecula. A non-contrast computed tomography (CT) scan showed increased soft tissue size on the lingual surface of the epiglottis. The biopsy revealed an ulcer base with fungus (spores with some budding).. Confirmed diagnosis: Subacute Histoplasmosis. Differential diagnosis includes: Subacute Histoplasmosis.
knowledge_fragments.title: Case report: Subacute Histoplasmosis

knowledge_fragments.content: Cutaneous manifestations are frequent and often early features of both Kawasaki disease (KD) and multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C). Although these conditions differ in epidemiology and triggers, they share overlapping clinical features and immune-mediated pathogenic mechanisms, making early recognition and differential diagnosis challenging. Dermatologic findings are particularly relevant, as they may represent the first clinical clue and precede severe systemic complications.
knowledge_fragments.title: Cutaneous Clues in Kawasaki Disease: Clinical Implications and Differential Diagnosis with Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children. > 1. Background

knowledge_fragments.content: Presentation: Treatment with agalsidase beta during pregnancy in Fabry disease.. Salient findings: life-threatening clinical consequences in the kidney, heart, and cerebrovascular system. Confirmed diagnosis: Fabry disease. Differential diagnosis includes: Fabry disease; lysosomal storage disease; multisystem progressive disease.
knowledge_fragments.title: Case report: Fabry disease

knowledge_fragments.content: Acute febrile neutrophilic dermatosis, also known as Sweet syndrome (SS) is a rare inflammatory skin disorder characterized by the appearance of erythematous papules, plaques or nodules, accompanied by fever and neutrophilic leukocytosis.
knowledge_fragments.title: Urticaria: A Narrative Overview of Differential Diagnosis. > 7. Other Inflammatory Conditions > 7.2. Sweet Syndrome

knowledge_fragments.content: Presentation: A 40-year-old man with skin phototype IV presented with a 1-month history of multiple reddish skin lesions located on the anterior chest, neck, and upper back. The patient reported photosensitivity and intermittent joint pain. He denied any history of prior drug intake. Physical examination of the skin revealed multiple erythematous, scaly papules and annular plaques, with some plaques exhibiting a peripheral rim of white scales.. Confirmed diagnosis: Subacute Cutaneous Lupus Erythematosus. Differential diagnosis includes: Subacute Cutaneous Lupus Erythematosus.
knowledge_fragments.title: Case report: Subacute Cutaneous Lupus Erythematosus
